name: CoreWeave, Inc.
blurb: CoreWeave is a neocloud — a GPU-specialist cloud provider that rents NVIDIA accelerator capacity to AI developers, research labs, and enterprises rather than offering the broad service catalogue of a hyperscaler. Founded in 2017 as a cryptocurrency mining operation and pivoted to GPU cloud in 2019, it operates more than 40 data centres with roughly 250,000 NVIDIA GPUs. Its commercial model is long-term capacity contracts — often three to seven years — which produce a large, predictable backlog but require heavy upfront debt-financed capital expenditure. CoreWeave went public on NASDAQ on 28 March 2025 at $40 per share, valuing the company at approximately $23 billion fully diluted. NVIDIA invested $2 billion in CoreWeave at $87.20 per share in January 2026, cementing the symbiotic relationship between the two companies.
recent: CoreWeave reported $5.1 billion in revenue for full-year 2025, up 170% year-on-year, with quarterly revenue reaching $1.57 billion in Q4. Microsoft accounted for approximately 67% of FY2025 revenue. OpenAI has contracted up to $22.4 billion in cumulative commitments, and Meta signed a $14.2 billion agreement through December 2031. Total remaining performance obligations represent roughly 13 years of revenue at current run rates. In April 2026, CoreWeave priced an upsized $3.5 billion convertible senior notes offering and announced a multi-year GPU capacity agreement with Anthropic.
